commit.message: Add more semi-colons
Add more semi-colons
Fix issue when parsing empty FASTQ reads #451
Handle edge cases that would cause parser to behave inconsistenly
Add official support for libsais library
Reduce the max buffer size from 16GB to 16MB
Fix mutually exclusive error when specifying -F together with -f; update documention for FASTA-continuous
Change max size of small index to 2GB when using SAIS
Add support for newer version of NCBI_VDB and replace NCBI_NGS with sra-tools
Add documentation for building with libsais
Use SRA libs only for the bowtie2-align binaries
Update SRA build recipe and dependencies in CMakeLists.txt
Add CMake support for building bowtie2 with libsais
Update documentation in preparation for release 2.5.3
Undo change that removed libdl from SRA-enabled builds
Remove librt when cross-compiling Windows on Linux
Disable warnings for variables that are set but unused
Remove whitespace character preventing the removal -lrt from LDLIBS
Potential fix for memory leaks when processing BAM files
Allow bowtie2 to continue trying after partial writes, use perror for write errors for better debugging
Fix an issue causing repetitive alignments for concordant reads to be overcounted
Allow tokenizer to trim whitespace around delimiter
Add support for toggling SAM Opt flags from the command line
Fix potential for overflow during tokenization
Fix simple test failures
Setup BWT output streams to throw an exception if error occurs during writing
Fix test failures on MacOS
Print the last successful mate parsed if mismatch in number of paired-end reads
Add new indexes to sidebar
Add announcement for new indexes
Rearrange indexes in sidebar
Update documentation in preparation for release of v2.5.4
Merge branch 'master' into bug_fixes
Update release date

+Building with SRA support
+
 As of version 2.3.5 bowtie2 now supports aligning SRA reads. Prepackaged
 builds will include a package that supports SRA. If you're building
 bowtie2 from source please make sure that the Java runtime is available
 on your system. You can then proceed with the build by running
 make sra-deps && make USE_SRA=1.
 
+Building with libsais support
+
+As of version 2.5.3 bowtie2 supports building indexes using the SAIS
+algorithm provided by libsais. SAIS is a state-of-the-art suffix array
+construction algorithm that will bring-forth a significant speed-up to
+the overall index building process. There is, however, the downside of a
+significant increase in memory usage compared to the persistent
+blockwise algorithm that bowtie2-build uses by default. When using SAIS
+small indexes can be built for inputs up to 2GB. The bowtie2-build
+wrapper will help determine the appropriate index type for uncompressed
+and gzipped inputs.
+
+To build bowtie2-build with libsais first make sure that the libsais
+submodule is available. This can be done in one of the following ways:
+
+-   first time cloning bowtie2 --
+    git clone --recursive https://github.com/BenLangmead/bowtie2.git
+-   existing checkout of bowtie2 --
+    git submodule init && git submodule update
+
+Issue the following command line to build libsais:
+
+-   with OpenMP support -- [g]make libsais USE_SAIS_OPENMP=1
+-   without OpenMP support -- [g]make libsais USE_SAIS=1
+
+The choice of using OpenMP will determine whether or not the algorithm
+runs multithreaded. The [-p/--threads] argument to bowtie2-build will be
+ignored when libsais is compiled without OpenMP support.
+
+Finally, building the bowtie2-build executable:
+
+-   with OpenMP support -- [g]make bowtie2-build-s USE_SAIS_OPENMP=1
+-   without OpenMP support -- [g]make bowtie2-build-s USE_SAIS=1
+
+Building with CMake
+
+To build Bowtie2 with SRA and libsais support issue the following
+command:
+
+-   cmake . -D USE_SRA=1 -D USE_SAIS=1 && cmake --build .
+
+CMake will take care of building and linking against the specified
+dependencies.
+
 Adding to PATH
 
 By adding your new Bowtie 2 directory to your PATH environment variable,

+## Version 2.5.4 - May 16, 2024 ##
+
+### bowtie2 ###
+   * Added `--sam-opt-config` command line option for toggling SAM Opt flags.

+
+## Version 2.5.3 - Jan 16, 2024 ##
+

+   * Fixed an issue causing `bowtie2` to crash when processing empty FASTQ records.
+   * Fixed an issue that would cause `bowtie2` to erroneously treat `-f` and `-F` as mutually exclusive.
+   * Add optional support for `libsais` to `bowtie2-build` for faster index building.
+     N.B. -- small indexes are capped at 2GB when using `libsais` as opposed to 4GB when using the

As of version 2.5.3 bowtie2 supports building indexes +using the SAIS algorithm provided by libsais. SAIS is a +state-of-the-art suffix array construction algorithm that will +bring-forth a significant speed-up to the overall index building +process. There is, however, the downside of a significant increase in +memory usage compared to the persistent blockwise algorithm that +bowtie2-build uses by default. When using SAIS small +indexes can be built for inputs up to 2GB. The +bowtie2-build wrapper will help determine the appropriate +index type for uncompressed and gzipped inputs.
